 State emergency: NY reports first measles-linked death in over 30 years. 

 Robotaxis: Who captures the most value in the burgeoning industry? 

 Resuming attacks? Oil edges up after U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 The midterm spread 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 Americans across the country will be heading to the polls today for midterm elections, which will determine whether President Trump has managed to retain Republican control of Congress. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives will be on the ballot, with members there serving two-year terms. Over in the Senate, 35 of the 100 seats are on the line, reflecting the chamber's staggered six-year cycle.

 Snapshot: More than 46M Americans have already voted early in the 2026 midterms, with record turnouts notched in several key battlegrounds. Midterm ballots also feature a wide slate of state-level and local offices, such as governors, attorneys general, and legislators, and even initiatives like wealth taxes and data center construction . The big news, however, will be coming from Capitol Hill, with prediction-market traders currently pushing the odds of a Democratic sweep of Congress above 75% .

A Democratic win in either chamber would freeze the administration's legislative priorities, effectively halting statutory efforts surrounding agendas like financial deregulation and crypto frameworks. Trade policy, however, would remain largely untouched as tariffs, export controls, and foreign trade investigations rely on executive powers. Energy and tech face a similar split: the White House can use executive authority to prioritize fossil-fuel leasing and tighten chip export curbs, while a divided Congress would defend clean-energy tax credits and use committees to intensify Big Tech antitrust scrutiny.  Historical analysis of the S&P 500 after midterms 

 Portfolio playbook: While there will be eyes on some of the big races in Maine, Michigan, Georgia, and Arizona, investors are considering what it might mean for their holdings. In a recent Seeking Alpha poll , half of the 871 participants said to stay the course in long-term allocations despite midterm swings, while nearly a third have built a cash cushion to reduce volatility or buy post-election dips. Out of the rest, 13% of subscribers are rebalancing their portfolios, while only 9% are actively playing election themes like energy, defense, and financials.
